job.style: a puzzle or game that uses the idea

passage: Rohan is designing a triangular garden patch for his school project. He knows the sides of the triangle are in the ratio 3:4:5, but he needs to find the actual lengths to calculate the area. He remembers that the perimeter is 60 cm, so he divides the perimeter by the sum of the ratio parts to find the common multiplier, which is 5. Thus, the sides are 15 cm, 20 cm, and 25 cm. To find the area, Rohan first calculates the semi-perimeter, s, which is half of the total perimeter, giving him 30 cm. He knows that Heron's formula is the square root of s(s-a)(s-b)(s-c). He carefully substitutes his values to get the square root of 30(15)(10)(5), which simplifies to 150 cm². Rohan also realizes that because this is a right-angled triangle, he could have simply used half the product of the two shorter sides. Finally, he considers a rhombus-shaped flower bed nearby. He knows the area of a rhombus is half the product of its diagonals, not just the product of the diagonals themselves. He measures the diagonals as 8 cm and 6 cm, calculating the area as 24 cm².

items.evidence: He remembers that the perimeter is 60 cm, so he divides the perimeter by the sum of the ratio parts to find the common multiplier, which is 5.
items.q: A triangle's sides are in the ratio 3:4:5 and its perimeter is 24 cm. What are its sides?
items.explain: 24 ÷ (3+4+5) = 2, so multiply each ratio part by 2.

wrong.why: takes the ratio numbers as the actual sides
splits the perimeter equally among three sides
copies Rohan's numbers from the passage

items.evidence: To find the area, Rohan first calculates the semi-perimeter, s, which is half of the total perimeter, giving him 30 cm.
items.q: A triangle has sides 7 cm, 8 cm and 9 cm. What value of s goes into Heron's formula?
items.explain: s is half the perimeter: (7+8+9) ÷ 2 = 12 cm.

wrong.why: thinks s means the full perimeter
takes the middle side as s
doubles the perimeter instead of halving it

items.evidence: Rohan also realizes that because this is a right-angled triangle, he could have simply used half the product of the two shorter sides.
items.q: Why could Rohan find his triangle's area without Heron's formula?
options: Its two shorter sides are base and height
Its longest side can act as the height
Its perimeter is a round number, 60 cm
Any one of its sides can be the height
items.explain: In a right-angled triangle the two shorter sides are base and height, so area = ½ × 15 × 20.

wrong.why: thinks height can be along a slanting side
picks a true detail that is not the reason
thinks height is always one of the sides

items.evidence: He knows the area of a rhombus is half the product of its diagonals, not just the product of the diagonals themselves.
items.q: A rhombus has diagonals of 10 cm and 4 cm. What is its area?
items.explain: Area of a rhombus is half the product of diagonals: ½ × 10 × 4 = 20 cm².

wrong.why: adds the diagonals instead of multiplying
